rationale: The same saying appears in both Gospels. In the BSB both say "none will be given it except the sign of" Jonah (Matthew 12:39 has "the prophet Jonah"; Luke 11:29 has "Jonah"), and the two judgment sayings match nearly word for word, ending "now One greater than Jonah is here" and "now One greater than Solomon is here" (Matthew 12:41-42; Luke 11:31-32). The type is parallel. The label is strong, not explicit, following conn-matt11-woes-luke10, where a near-verbatim synoptic parallel is graded the same way: neither Gospel cites the other. The differences can be checked. Where Matthew explains the sign by Jonah's "three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish" (12:40), Luke has "as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation" (11:30). Luke puts the Queen of the South before the men of Nineveh, and places the saying about the unclean spirit earlier (11:24-26), where Matthew has it after (12:43-45). Matthew also repeats the core saying at 16:4.
